cards.name: Bullish Candle
cards.desc: Price closed above where it opened. Buyers were in control for this candle. A larger body is read as stronger conviction.
cards.note: Color alone means nothing without context. Traders read a bullish candle inside a downtrend differently from one at key support.

cards.name: Bearish Candle
cards.desc: Price closed below where it opened. Sellers were in control for this candle. A larger body is read as stronger selling pressure.
cards.note: In an uptrend, a bearish candle at support is read as a pullback. The same candle at resistance after a rally is read as a warning.

cards.name: Marubozu
cards.desc: No wicks. Price opened at one extreme and closed at the other. No wicks means price did not trade back from either extreme during the candle.
cards.note: A bullish marubozu is read as buyers in control for the whole candle; a bearish marubozu as sellers in control.

cards.name: Doji
cards.desc: Open and close are nearly identical. Neither side won. Traders read it as a pause. The longer the wicks, the more contested the price.
cards.note: Traders read a doji as indecision and look left for context. Common variants: Standard, Long-Legged, Dragonfly, Gravestone.

cards.name: Hammer
cards.desc: Long lower wick, small body near the top. Sellers pushed price hard — buyers fought back and closed near the open. The wick is the story. The body color is irrelevant.
cards.note: Traders look for it after a downtrend or at support. Body color is not what defines it. Same shape as Hanging Man — location defines how it is read.

cards.name: Hanging Man
cards.desc: Long lower wick, small body near the top. Identical shape to the Hammer. At the top of an uptrend it is read as buyers failing to hold gains, and as a possible sign that sellers are entering.
cards.note: Traders look for it after an uptrend or at resistance. Body color does not define how it is read; location does.

cards.name: Inverted Hammer
cards.desc: Long upper wick, small body near the bottom. Buyers tried to push higher — sellers rejected the move. Traders read the attempt as buyer interest and wait for confirmation.
cards.note: Traders look for it after a downtrend or at support. Body color does not change how it is read. Same shape as Shooting Star — location defines how it is read.

cards.name: Shooting Star
cards.desc: Long upper wick, small body near the bottom. Buyers pushed price up hard — sellers rejected the move and closed near the open. A green body does not make this bullish.
cards.note: Traders look for it after an uptrend or at resistance. Same shape as Inverted Hammer — location defines how it is read.

cards.name: Shadows & Wicks
cards.desc: The thin lines above and below the candle body. Upper wick = buyers pushed price here but got rejected. Lower wick = sellers pushed price here but got rejected. Wicks show the battlefield.
cards.note: Traders mark long wicks at key levels as places where price was refused, and watch those levels on later approaches.

cards.name: Engulfing Pattern
cards.desc: A candle that completely engulfs the prior candle's body. Bullish engulfing: large green candle swallows prior red. Bearish engulfing: large red candle swallows prior green. One side overwhelmed the other.
cards.note: Traders look for it at key levels after an extended move. A larger engulf is read as a stronger one, and volume is checked alongside.

cards.name: Harami Pattern
cards.desc: A small candle contained entirely within the prior candle's body. The large candle sets the range — the small candle is read as momentum slowing.
cards.note: Traders read it as a weaker sign than the engulfing and wait for the next candle. Bullish harami is looked for after a downtrend, bearish harami after an uptrend.

cards.name: Kicker Pattern
cards.desc: Two candles in opposite directions with a gap between them. Traders read it as a complete shift in sentiment, often around news.
cards.note: Bullish kicker: red candle followed by green that gaps above. Bearish kicker: green followed by red that gaps below.

cards.name: Morning Star
cards.desc: Three candles: a large bearish candle, a small indecision candle, then a large bullish candle closing above the midpoint of the first. Traders read it as a possible reversal and as selling losing momentum.
cards.note: The middle candle is the pivot, where the move stalls. The third candle is what traders look to as confirmation.

cards.name: Evening Star
cards.desc: Three candles: a large bullish candle, a small indecision candle, then a large bearish candle closing below the midpoint of the first. The mirror of Morning Star.
cards.note: Traders look for it at resistance after an extended uptrend. The third candle closes well into the body of the first.

cards.name: Three White Soldiers
cards.desc: Three consecutive bullish candles, each opening within the prior body and closing progressively higher. Read as sustained buying pressure across three sessions.
cards.note: Traders read it by location: after a downtrend as a possible shift, after a long uptrend with caution about exhaustion.

cards.name: Three Black Crows
cards.desc: Three consecutive bearish candles, each opening within the prior body and closing progressively lower. The mirror of Three White Soldiers. Read as sustained selling.
cards.note: Traders look for it after an extended uptrend. Each candle has a small or no lower wick, which is read as sellers holding control through the session.

cards.name: Piercing / Dark Cloud
cards.desc: Two-candle reversal patterns. Piercing: bearish candle followed by bullish that closes above the midpoint of the first (bullish). Dark Cloud Cover: opposite direction (bearish).
cards.note: The key requirement: the second candle must close above (or below) the 50% midpoint of the first candle's body. A close short of the midpoint does not count as the pattern.

cards.name: Double Top
cards.desc: Price reaches the same high twice and fails to break through. Two rejections at resistance. A break of the neckline is what traders treat as confirmation.
cards.note: Traders measure the distance from the tops to the neckline to set a projected target after a break, and watch for lower volume on the second top.

cards.name: Double Bottom
cards.desc: Price tests the same low twice and holds. Two rejections at support. A break of the neckline to the upside is what traders treat as confirmation.
cards.note: The mirror of Double Top. A second bottom slightly higher than the first is read as less selling pressure.

cards.name: Triple Top
cards.desc: Three failed attempts to break through the same resistance level. Traders read each failure as adding weight to the rejection.
cards.note: A third test is read as carrying more weight than a double top. Traders often treat a longer formation as more significant.

cards.name: Head & Shoulders
cards.desc: Three peaks: a smaller left shoulder, a higher head, a smaller right shoulder. The neckline connects the two troughs. A break below the neckline is what traders treat as the reversal signal.
cards.note: One of the most widely recognized reversal patterns. Traders often look for volume to peak on the left shoulder and decline through the head and right shoulder.

cards.name: Rounding Top
cards.desc: A gradual, curved peak, read as slow distribution over time. Unlike sharp reversals, it develops slowly and is read as buyers losing control gradually.
cards.note: Looked for on longer timeframes. Traders read the slow curve as distribution: selling into strength over weeks or months.

cards.name: Bull Flag
cards.desc: A sharp upward move (the pole) followed by a controlled, downward-sloping consolidation (the flag). Traders read the flag as a pause, with buyers regrouping.
cards.note: Traders prefer a tight, orderly flag, and look for volume to fall during the flag and rise on a breakout.

cards.name: Bear Flag
cards.desc: A sharp downward move followed by a controlled, upward-sloping consolidation. Traders read the consolidation as a relief bounce, with sellers regrouping.
cards.note: Mirror of Bull Flag. The upward drift in the flag is read as sellers allowing a relief bounce.

cards.name: Pennant
cards.desc: A sharp move followed by a symmetrical triangle consolidation — converging trendlines forming a small symmetrical triangle. Price coils tighter inside the triangle.
cards.note: Similar to a flag but with converging lines rather than parallel. Traders watch for a break in the direction of the original move.

cards.name: Wedge
cards.desc: Two converging trendlines both moving in the same direction. Rising wedge (bearish): higher highs and higher lows compressing upward. Falling wedge (bullish): lower highs and lower lows compressing downward.
cards.note: A rising wedge slopes up and a falling wedge slopes down, with the lines converging in both. Traders read the rising wedge as bearish and the falling wedge as bullish.

cards.name: Ascending Triangle
cards.desc: Flat resistance at the top, rising support below. Buyers keep making higher lows while sellers defend a fixed level. Traders read this as pressure building under resistance.
cards.note: The flat top is where sellers are read to be positioned. Each higher low is read as buyers pressing against them. A break above is what traders watch for.

cards.name: Descending Triangle
cards.desc: Flat support at the bottom, declining resistance above. Sellers keep making lower highs while buyers defend a fixed level. Mirror of Ascending Triangle.
cards.note: The flat bottom is where buyers are read to be positioned. Each lower high is read as sellers pressing against them. A break below is what traders watch for.

cards.name: Symmetrical Triangle
cards.desc: Converging trendlines with lower highs and higher lows. Neither side has taken control. Price coils tighter.
cards.note: Traders do not assume a direction and wait for the break. Contracting volume during formation and expanding volume on the break is what many look for.

cards.name: Support & Resistance
cards.desc: Support: a price level where buying has historically overwhelmed selling. Resistance: where selling has historically overwhelmed buying. These levels exist because traders remember them.
cards.note: A broken support level is often treated as resistance afterwards, and a broken resistance level as support. This is called a role reversal.

cards.name: Gap
cards.desc: When price opens significantly higher or lower than the prior close, leaving an unfilled area on the chart. Gaps are read as a sudden shift in sentiment, often around news or overnight events.
cards.note: Gap N Go: price continues in the gap direction. Gap Fill: price reverses to close the gap. Which of the two a trader is looking for depends on context.

cards.name: Trend vs Range
cards.desc: Trend: price making consistent higher highs and higher lows (uptrend) or lower highs and lower lows (downtrend). Range: price oscillating between defined support and resistance without direction.
cards.note: Traders ask before each trade whether the market is trending or ranging, since the answer decides which setup they look for.
